slides.title: Sources of error and interpretation
bullets: If urine stands for more than an hour after collection, red cells lyse and casts break down.
Kurbonova: normally up to 5–6 white cells and 0–2 red cells per field, no casts; Aripova writes that red cells are not normally present (except in samples taken during menstruation).
Dirt on cover glasses and slides and foreign objects from the air (wool, pollen, cotton fibres) may be mistaken for sediment elements.

In the Nechiporenko method the formed elements in 1 mL of urine are counted in a Goryaev chamber; calculation formulas and reference values differ between the sources, so follow the laboratory’s instructions.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: Wear single-use gloves when handling specimens; after work wash the hands with soap or wipe them with an alcohol solution.
Balance the tubes in the centrifuge; close the lid and do not open it until the machine has stopped completely.
Put used containers, tubes and slides into a disinfectant solution (concentration and time according to the regulation in force).

slides.title: Example: Nechiporenko count
bullets: Formula: x (per 1 µL of sediment) = A ÷ V, where A is the cells counted and V the volume of the ruling counted, µL. N (per 1 ml of urine) = x × sediment volume (µL) ÷ urine centrifuged (ml) [1, p. 44].
slides.ex: Example (Aripova [2, p. 99]): 10 ml urine, 1 ml sediment, 100 large Goryaev squares (0.4 µL) → N = A × 250.

slides.title: Urine sediment
slides.caption: Under a microscope, pus cells appear as small, spherical cells with a multi-lobed nucleus. They are a key part of the body's immune response to infection or inflammation. Pus cells in urine indicate an ongoing immune response in the urinary tract.
slides.credit: Photo: Ajay Kumar Chaurasiya, CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

slides.title: Urine sediment
slides.caption: From the source: “Urine microscopy for analysis of urine sediments. Renal tubular epithelial cell casts (a) and muddy brown granular casts (b) suggest acute tubular injury/necrosis (ATN) as the cause of AKI.
slides.credit: Photo: Mohsenin V., CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

slides.title: Urine sediment
slides.caption: White cell casts are generally seen in acute interstitial nephritis or acute pyelonephritis (c). A red cell cast denotes glomerular disease such as glomerulonephritis or small vessel vasculitis (d).”
slides.credit: Photo: Mohsenin V., CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
